title: Sustained antidepressant-like effects of psychedelics through 5-HT2AR–β-arrestin signaling
title_zh: 通过5-HT2AR–β-受体酶抑制信号产生的持久抗抑郁样效应
abstract: Psychedelics produce long-lasting antidepressant effects, but their hallucinogenic properties limit clinical use. Using structure-guided design of 5-HT2AR-β-arrestin-biased agonists, we identified β-arrestin signaling as a critical driver of prolonged antidepressant-like effects in mice. Here we show that the slow-dissociation kinetics of lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD) enable progressive accumulation of 5-HT2AR engagement during repeated low-dose administration, approaching the receptor occupancy achieved by an acute high dose while avoiding its high peak concentration. This kinetic separation sustains β-arrestin signaling while limiting robust Gαq-mediated Ca2+ responses. Consistent with this framework, repeated low-dose LSD and repeated low-dose psilocybin pretreatment followed by a high-dose psychedelic challenge produced sustained antidepressant-like behavioral effects in mice. In parallel, these regimens produced no detectable psychedelic-associated behavioral disruption in mice and cynomolgus macaques. Together, these findings uncover the signaling basis of sustained psychedelic efficacy and provide a rational framework for developing nonhallucinogenic psychedelic therapies for psychiatric disorders.
abstract_zh: 迷幻剂产生持久的抗抑郁样效果，但其致幻特性限制了临床应用。利用5-HT2AR-β-受体酶抑制设计的结构引导方法，我们确定β-受体酶信号是小鼠中持久抗抑郁样效应的关键驱动因素。在此，我们展示赖酸二乙基酰胺（LSD）缓慢的解离动力学使得在重复低剂量给药期间5-HT2AR结合逐步累积，接近单次高剂量实现的受体占用率，同时避免了其高峰浓度。这种动力学分离持续β-受体酶信号，同时限制了强效Gαq介导的Ca2+反应。与这一框架一致，小鼠和猕猴在重复低剂量LSD和重复低剂量裸盖菌素预处理后，随后给予高剂量迷幻剂挑战，均产生了持久的抗抑郁样行为效应。与此同时，这些方案在小鼠和猕猴中未检测到与迷幻相关的行为紊乱。综上，这些发现揭示了迷幻剂持续疗效的信号基础，并为开发精神疾病非致幻迷幻疗法提供了合理框架。
